name: CommuniQate
author: Niek Poorthuis

sections.description:
This is the official CommuniQate plugin. Add a floating chat widget across your website or place callouts directly inside pages and posts. Your visitors reach your business through WhatsApp, Instagram or email, and you answer them in CommuniQate.

To use the plugin you need a CommuniQate account with a chat widget or callout. You manage texts, colors, layouts and channels in CommuniQate. In WordPress you only enter the Widget ID and choose where the callout appears. Changes in CommuniQate appear when visitors reload the page.

Use the CommuniQate callout block in WordPress 5.8 and newer, or place [communiqate_widget id="WIDGET_ID"] in the classic editor or a page builder. Replace WIDGET_ID with the ID of your callout. Multiple callouts can share a page, including alongside a floating chat widget. Every widget is a placement in the page, and the shared embed script loads once and creates an iframe for each of them.

Important: the widget is loaded from CommuniQate, a third-party service. See “External services” below for what this means. By using this plugin, you agree to the CommuniQate Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. These apply to the use of the widget and to any data that is collected while it runs.

For more information, visit the CommuniQate website: https://communiqate.nl.

External services

This plugin connects to CommuniQate, the service that provides the widgets. The widgets cannot work without it.

  • On pages with a floating widget or callout, the browser of your visitor loads the widget script from https://widgets.communiqate.nl/assets/scripts/widget/v2/embed.js and each widget iframe from https://widget.communiqate.nl. The callout block also loads these resources when showing its preview in the editor. This sends the Widget ID and the data every browser sends with a request, such as the IP address of the visitor and the address of your site, to CommuniQate.
  • When you save the Widget ID, the plugin asks https://widget.communiqate.nl whether a widget with that Widget ID exists. This sends the Widget ID and, as with every request WordPress makes, the address of your site to CommuniQate.

The service is provided by CommuniQate. Terms of Use: https://www.communiqate.nl/legaal/algemene-voorwaarden. Privacy Policy: https://www.communiqate.nl/legaal/privacy-cookies.
sections.installation:
1. In your WordPress dashboard, go to Plugins > Add New, search for “CommuniQate” and click Install Now. You can also download the plugin from WordPress.org and upload the ZIP file through Plugins > Add New > Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin.
  3. In CommuniQate, open the website widgets page and copy the Widget ID of your widget.
  4. In your WordPress dashboard, click CommuniQate in the menu, paste the Widget ID and click Save Changes.

The floating widget now appears on every page of your site. Existing settings continue to work after updating the plugin.

For an inline callout:

  1. Create a callout in CommuniQate and copy its Widget ID.
  2. Add the CommuniQate callout block to a page and paste the ID, or use [communiqate_widget id="WIDGET_ID"] in a shortcode-compatible editor.
  3. Save the page. The callout appears in that position and stays in sync with CommuniQate.

The site-wide Widget ID is optional. Leave it empty if you only use callouts.
sections.faq:
What is the CommuniQate plugin for?

The CommuniQate plugin loads CommuniQate website widgets on your WordPress site, so visitors can contact your business through WhatsApp, Instagram or email directly from your site.

Where do I find my Widget ID?

On the website widgets page in CommuniQate. A Widget ID looks like xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx.

Do I need to update existing widgets?

No. Your saved site-wide Widget ID and existing installation codes keep working. Adding callouts does not replace the floating widget.

Can I use a callout more than once?

Yes. You can place the same or different callouts multiple times with blocks or shortcodes. Use the ID of a callout for these placements.

Where do I edit the callout design?

In CommuniQate. WordPress stores only the Widget ID and its position in your content. The block preview loads from CommuniQate and disables links while editing.

The widget does not appear on my site. What can I do?

  • Check that a Widget ID is saved on the CommuniQate page in your WordPress dashboard.
  • If you use a caching plugin, clear its cache.
  • If a plugin on your site delays, combines or rewrites scripts, exclude the CommuniQate script (widgets.communiqate.nl) from it.
  • Open the console of your browser on your site. Messages from the widget start with [CommuniQate].

Does this plugin rely on a third-party service?

Yes, this plugin loads the widget from CommuniQate. The widget depends on the availability of this service. You need a CommuniQate account and a Widget ID to show the widget on your site.

Where can I find the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy of CommuniQate?

The Terms of Use are at https://www.communiqate.nl/legaal/algemene-voorwaarden and the Privacy Policy is at https://www.communiqate.nl/legaal/privacy-cookies.
sections.changelog:
1.1.0

  • 2026.11.07
  • Added [communiqate_widget id=”WIDGET_ID”] for inline callouts in pages and page builders
  • Added a CommuniQate callout block with a live iframe preview in WordPress 5.8 and newer
  • Uses Block API 3 on WordPress 6.3 and newer, with an API 2 fallback for WordPress 5.8–6.2
  • Callouts use the shared embed script and remain centrally managed in CommuniQate
  • Uses the v2 embed script to avoid long-lived v1 browser caches while preserving existing widget IDs
  • Multiple callouts work on the same page, including alongside the floating chat widget
  • The script loads once per page and works without a site-wide Widget ID
  • Existing Widget IDs and installation codes remain supported
  • Updated settings and instructions for sites that only use callouts
  • The site-wide chat widget is placed like every other widget, as a container marked as the chat, and the shared script tag is the same on every page, as in the installation code from CommuniQate
  • Added regression tests for legacy widgets, shortcode/block rendering, validation and script loading

1.0.1

  • 2026.10.28
  • Fixed the widget not loading on WordPress 7.0 and newer
  • The Widget ID is checked when saving, so a Widget ID that was pasted twice or cut off is no longer saved
  • When saving, the plugin asks CommuniQate whether a widget with the Widget ID exists, and shows a warning when CommuniQate cannot confirm it
  • The dashboard and the plugins page show a notice as long as no Widget ID has been entered
  • The settings page has a main heading and the Widget ID field has a label, for screen readers
  • The readme is now in English

1.0

  • 2024.10.22
  • Initial release
